extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of philosophy, aesthetics, and music theory; composers and educated general readers
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt from a philosophical treatise discussing the metaphysical significance of history and music, laying out principles about what makes history valuable and what constitutes musical form, expression, and effect. Useful as normative/aesthetic criteria for judging musical composition, historic monuments, and philosophical approaches to death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of history as universal consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: History is to be regarded as the rational consciousness of the human race; only through history does a nation become completely conscious of itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: History connects present generations with the past, allowing understanding of the present and anticipation of the future; gaps in history are like gaps in individual recollective self-consciousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of writing and monuments
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing and stone monuments serve to restore unity to the consciousness of the human race and to speak to remote descendants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monuments/structures (pyramids, temples, palaces) and inscriptions are intended to address posterity; durable construction and inscriptions (e.g., hieroglyphics, paintings) are means to preserve continuity; it is shameful to destroy or disfigure such works for low utilitarian ends; written monuments have less elemental risk but more to fear from barbarians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music acts directly upon the will (emotional expression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Music acts directly upon the will — i.e., the feelings, passions, and emotions of the hearer — and does not express Ideas (grades of objectification of the will) but the will itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike other arts, music's object is immediate feeling; this underpins its greater power and explains why music can produce strong emotional changes without representational content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words are subordinate to music
rubrics_metrics.description: Words are and remain for the music a foreign addition, of subordinate value; if words are incorporated they must assume an entirely subordinate position and adapt completely to the music.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Music need not rely on poetry or libretto; when used together the libretto should be written for the music rather than music for the libretto; composers use words as stimulus for musical imagination but should keep music primary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music reveals inner significance of drama
rubrics_metrics.description: Music discloses the most profound ultimate and secret significance of the feeling expressed in words or the action presented in an opera; it is the soul of the drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Music expresses the inner necessity and ultimate meaning of incidents and persons, providing the spectator with an indistinct but essential feeling that shapes dramatic appreciation; yet music remains indifferent to stage material and expresses passions uniformly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumental music expresses passions abstractly
rubrics_metrics.description: Purely instrumental music (e.g., a Beethoven symphony) presents human passions and emotions 'in abstracto' — their mere form without particularisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listeners may imaginatively particularise these emotions, but comprehension and enjoyment don't require extra-narrative representation; this abstractness is a feature, not a defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical/arithmetical basis of harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: All harmony depends upon the coincidence of vibrations: rational relations (small-number ratios) yield consonance (coincidence), irrational or large-number relations yield dissonance (resistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theory connects the physical vibration relations to perceptual consonance/dissonance and underpins musical ordering; music thereby makes numerical relations sensible rather than conceptual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consonance as satisfaction, dissonance as resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Dissonance is the natural type of what resists our will; consonance is the type of satisfaction of the will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because numerical relations admit innumerable degrees, music can portray all finer shades of satisfaction/dissatisfaction; the emotional effect of chords links to will-based metaphysics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melody consists of rhythmical and harmonious elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Melody consists of two elements: the rhythmical (quantitative — duration) and the harmonious (qualitative — pitch); rhythm is the essential element, and complete melody requires both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In notation the rhythmical depends on vertical (perpendicular) organization (beats/measures) and the harmonious on horizontal (pitch) lines; both must interact properly for melody to arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm analogous to symmetry (architecture analogy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhythm is in time what symmetry is in space; architecture and music are extremes whose analogy rests on rhythm/symmetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Musical structure involves periods, parts, repetition and hierarchical division (beats→bars→periods→parts→movements); typical movement counts: concerto/sonata ≈ 3, symphony ≈ 4, mass ≈ 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melody as alternating disunion and reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature of melody consists in the constantly renewed disunion and reconciliation of the rhythmical and harmonious elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A melodic 'rest' (satisfaction) must occur when harmonic arrival coincides with an accented beat; mismatches produce disquiet; suspension (delayed resolution) heightens longing and makes resolution more satisfying; example: cadence requires the preceding dominant-seventh chord.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of dissonance to avoid satiation
rubrics_metrics.description: A succession of merely consonant chords would be satiating and wearisome; dissonances must be introduced (though they disquiet) in order to be resolved into consonances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Musical feeling depends on alternation of more or less disquieting (dissonant) and more or less satisfying (consonant) chords; at bottom music reduces to two fundamental chord types: the dissonant seventh and the consonant triad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major and minor express general moods
rubrics_metrics.description: Music has two general keys: the major (serenity or healthiness) and the minor (sadness or oppression); music must always be in one of the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The minor key functions as a sign of pain that is neither physically painful nor conventional; national and stylistic tendencies affect key choice (e.g., northern/Russian prevalence of minor, French allegro often in minor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Soprano as natural bearer of melody
rubrics_metrics.description: The musical ear prefers the highest note rather than the loudest, so the soprano naturally delivers the melody; the bass is much lower and cannot naturally present the melody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bass must remain far below the upper parts (generally not within an octave), is inflexible and governed by rigid rules; a melody assigned to bass is usually an inverted bass (counterpoint) and is unnatural, requiring accompaniment (a 'second fundamental bass').

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental spacing rule for bass and harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: The bass must be at a much greater distance below the three upper parts than they have between themselves; it must never approach nearer than at most within an octave of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This spacing explains why correct triads sit in the third octave from the fundamental; extended harmony (widely separated bass) is more powerful and beautiful than close harmony (used mainly for instrumental limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal temperament introduces harmonic impurity
rubrics_metrics.description: When the key-note is changed the same note assumes different functional roles ('actors' taking roles); the unavoidable impurity of every harmonic system is introduced by equal temperament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing keys exposes that notes 'play roles' that may not perfectly fit them; equal temperament trades pure intervals for the practicality of transposition, producing compromise in purity of intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music flatters the will to live (ethical/aesthetic implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Music flatters the will to live because it exhibits to it its nature, deludes it with the image of its success, and at the end expresses its satisfaction and contentment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an interpretive (metaphysical) judgement about music's ethical/aesthetic effect — music presents images of satisfaction which console the will; reference drawn to ancient texts (e.g., Vedas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy and religion as antidotes to the fear of death
rubrics_metrics.description: All religious and philosophical systems are principally directed to comforting us concerning the certainty of death introduced by reflective reason; some systems (Brahmanism, Buddhism) do this more effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrines that teach a consistent metaphysical ground (e.g., regarding the self as Brahm) better enable calm acceptance of death; weak/untenable early teachings (e.g., arising from poor cosmologies) can make later stable understanding and comfort impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger of instilling untenable early conceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is hazardous to force upon a person weak and untenable conceptions about origin or immortality in early education, because when reflection matures the person may be incapable of taking up correct and stable conceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: social and intellectual consequences (e.g., certain social groups sinking to materialism or 'bestialism') when stable metaphysical comfort is absent; stresses the pedagogical/ethical responsibility in teaching.
